name: Sumitomo Chemical India Ltd
title: Sumitomo Chemical India Ltd - 542920 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record FY26 profitability (PAT INR543 cr, up 7%) on 3% revenue growth; supply-side signals are mostly inventory build and a modest capex pipeline, with FY27 margins guided as cost-pass-through dependent and monsoon-exposed.

utilisation.quote: We enter FY '27 with production running at full capacity and no supply chain constraints.

capex.quote: we want to reconfirm our commitment to invest in infrastructure for expanding our manufacturing portfolio

triggers.label: Agro business growth ~5-6%, all volume
triggers.quote: if you look at our pure agro business, it has grown roughly in the range of 5% -6%, and almost everything through volume

summary.headline: Sumitomo Chemical India posted record FY26 profit: PAT up 7% to INR543 crore on revenue up 3% to INR3,238 crore, EBITDA margin 20.7%.
summary.overview: FY26 was a difficult industry year (excess monsoon, regulatory curbs on biologicals and PGRs, West Asia tension), yet the company reported record absolute profit and margins. Q4 revenue rose 1% to INR684 crore with EBITDA up 12% to INR134 crore, helped by a 223 bps gross margin expansion. Management flagged FY27 monsoon risk (IMD forecast 92% of LPA), rupee and input cost pressure, and is passing costs through via repeated price hikes. Board and management succession takes effect 1 September 2026, with Dr. Suresh Ramachandran becoming Managing Director.

financial_highlights.change: gross profit +6% YoY; gross margin +107 bps

financial_highlights.metric: Net worth / cash and liquid investments (31 Mar 2026)
financial_highlights.value: INR3,394 crore net worth; ~INR2,113 crore cash and liquid investments

financial_highlights.change: vs 89 days a year ago; receivable days 83 vs 91

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Domestic revenue grew 4% YoY in both Q4 and FY26; branded formulations rose to 81% of domestic sales from 79%. Specialty products are about 30% of domestic revenue; products launched in the last 3 years contribute about 8% of domestic revenue.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue fell 7% in Q4 and 1% for FY26 on shipment timing and softer demand in some markets; branded products are 40% of export revenue. Container constraints (including to Africa) are seen as episodic.

segments.name: Insecticides
segments.commentary: Largest product group at 41% of FY26 revenue; demand was hit by excess monsoon rains in August to October.

segments.name: Herbicides
segments.commentary: Grew 87% YoY in Q4 and 19% for FY26, driven by flumioxazin (soybean), Lentigo (rice) and Mera 71 (glyphosate). No herbicide returns from channel in FY26.

segments.name: Metal phosphates
segments.commentary: Grew 16% in Q4 and 11% for FY26.

segments.name: PGR and biologicals
segments.commentary: PGR decline driven by gibberellic acid after poor grape season; biologicals affected by regulatory approval gaps from about June 2025 to Nov-Dec 2025. Biologicals are 8-10% of revenue.

segments.name: Animal nutrition
segments.commentary: Revenue fell from INR65.3 crore in Q4 FY25 to INR37.5 crore in Q4 FY26. Company is restarting distribution of some products; margin about 4-5%.

segments.name: Custom synthesis (sales to parent)
segments.commentary: Roughly INR100-150 crore annually; management expects FY27 sales of INR110-130 crore, with growth from FY28 onwards.

guidance_outlook: FY27 described as cautiously optimistic; Q1 FY27 looks constructive, while Q2 and H2 depend on monsoon and geopolitics.

Price increases taken on 15 March, 1 April and 1 May 2026, with a further increase considered for 1 June; management expects about 10-15% cost escalation on a large scale, and 20-25% on some products.
Price realisation improved from late March, but management says margin impact could be net neutral or plus or minus a few percentage points.
No incremental revenue from new capex expected in FY27; new Dahej capex (INR150 crore) expected to contribute mainly from FY28-FY29.
Plants running at full capacity, with supply planned on a normal kharif season.
capex_capacity: Dahej INR150 crore project, expected to commercialise in about 2 years; second and further projects to be announced roughly yearly, with each of similar size.
Capex is being executed at Bhavnagar, Tarapur and Dahej; infrastructure progressing well, with commercialisation timelines dependent on parent-company regulatory approvals in export markets.
India elevated by parent SCC to the same tier as Japan, Brazil, North America and Europe for early-stage trials; 2 molecules received for Indian trials.
Management is evaluating high-purity semiconductor chemicals with the parent's ICTM department; an official announcement is expected soon.
Inventory built ahead of kharif: packaging and raw materials held beyond the usual ~90 days because of supply and lead-time risk.
demand_pricing: Management says FY26 agro business grew about 5-6%, almost entirely from volume; pricing was stable for the full year.
IMD forecasts the southwest monsoon at 92% of LPA (below normal); NOAA indicates 82% probability of El Nino during May-July.

Royalty arrangement: a small royalty to the parent applies only to 2-3 products where the company may now buy technicals externally; an annual report cap of INR2 crore is planned and the actual amount is expected to be lower.
Competitive pricing risk: management said it would have to reduce prices if competitors cut prices, and channel buying ahead of price increases inflated Q4 herbicide volumes.
Management said agrochemicals are a small share of farmer cost and that fertiliser supply, not agrochemical price, is the main variable for cropping patterns.

qa_highlights.question: Should FY27 margins be seen as flattish or declining, given monsoon, Gulf conflict and cost pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are considered sustainable and are being protected through repeated price increases; it cannot control raw material, freight or solvent costs, so it is passing them on as they arise.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory and working capital outlook for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was deliberately built in Q4 because packaging and raw material lead times rose (for example, packaging from 4 days to 8 days); management expects this to protect supply.

qa_highlights.question: Which new molecules could launch in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: TopGrain, a biostimulant from SBC, is registered and expected to launch in the coming kharif; one more product awaits registration and would be launched in FY27 if approved.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of Q4 and FY26 growth between volume and price?
qa_highlights.answer: Agro growth of about 5-6% for FY26 was volume-led; pricing was stable for the full year. Q4 herbicide growth was mainly volume, with some channel pre-buying.

qa_highlights.question: Scope and timing of the next capex at Dahej and the parent-approved products?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR150 crore Dahej project is progressing and is expected in about 2 years. Further projects are expected about yearly, but details are business-confidential; the next one may be a more integrated intermediate rather than a KSM.

qa_highlights.question: How much cash will fund capex, and will R&D need parent support?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the existing R&D team will handle the work with no capital or manpower needed from Japan, and that much of the capex will be funded from Indian cash reserves.

risks_watch: Monsoon outcome (IMD 92% of LPA, El Nino risk) and the kharif distribution through September.

Input cost inflation (packaging, solvents, naphtha-linked raw materials, freight) and rupee depreciation; the company says FX impact is broadly neutral because exports and imports are both about USD 70-80 million.
Fertiliser availability could shift cropping patterns; competitive price cuts if the war de-escalates.
Export volumes depend on logistics and customer ability to pay; container constraints were seen into early FY27.
Regulatory approvals from parent-company export markets could delay capex commercialisation timelines.
Channel inventory levels after pre-buying in Q4 FY26 could weigh on Q1 FY27 demand.
Leadership transition from 1 September 2026 (Dr. Suresh Ramachandran as MD, Chetan Shah as proposed non-executive Chairman).
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and on the leadership handover, but cautious on FY27, with repeated references to monsoon, geopolitics and cost uncertainty. Management was evasive on specific FY27 margin, volume and capex-size numbers, citing business confidentiality and the dynamic situation.
key_quotes: We delivered highest ever profitability performance in financial year '26, highest ever absolute terms and highest ever margin terms.
Overall, for FY '27, we are cautiously optimistic of the upcoming season based on the situations I described above.
And we will do the same thing continuously to ensure that margins are sustainable.
We have promised the sales team that no order of the customer will be turned down.

adds.what: INR150 crore Dahej project (new capacity, commercialisation in about 2 years)

growth.why: FY26 revenue grew 3% and FY27 guidance is cautious: no incremental revenue from new capex in FY27, with the INR150 crore Dahej project contributing mainly from FY28-FY29, and growth relies on price hikes (10-15% cost escalation passed through) and a monsoon forecast at 92% of LPA.

mgmt.note: Dr. Suresh Ramachandran becomes Managing Director effective 1 September 2026 as part of board and management succession; no specific growth plan stated in the brief.
